items.title: No Surprises Act defaults may be costing self-funded employers - Insurance Business
items.reason: The article addresses operational and financial impacts of No Surprises Act implementation on self-funded employers, which relates to how the rule affects healthcare payment processes and employer liability—directly relevant to revenue-cycle teams managing balance-billing compliance and claim processing.
items.summary: The No Surprises Act's implementation may be creating financial exposure for self-funded employers through defaults in compliance or claim processing, according to Insurance Business reporting. Self-funded employers, which directly bear the financial risk of healthcare claims, may be experiencing cost increases or claim payment issues related to how the No Surprises Act's balance-billing protections and dispute resolution processes are being applied. This affects revenue-cycle operations for employers and their administrators who must ensure proper claim adjudication under the Act's requirements. The impact matters because improper handling of No Surprises Act rules can result in unexpected costs, regulatory exposure, and operational inefficiencies in claims management.
